hard_case: the mock is a `jest.spyOn` of a module object, not an owner parameter, so the spec withholds the strong mock grade although the argument pin discriminates

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; jest 30.5.2, ts-jest 29.4.14, typescript 5.9.3; edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: `send` is called with `order 8` instead of `order 7`

reasoning: `announceMail(id)` calls `mailer.send("order " + id)` on a module object; the edit sends `order 8`. The test spies with `const send = jest.spyOn(mailer, "send")`, calls `announceMail(7)` and pins `expect(send).toHaveBeenCalledWith("order 7")`, which fails. RIPR-SPEC-0247 rule 4 (decision 10, amending example 5): `mailer` is an exported top-level `const`, the owner's only call is the changed `mailer.send(...)`, and the test body is only the spy, the one owner call and the assertion, so no other call can reach the spy and the literal pin reads `exposed`.
